tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.blurb: A cluster of huts and a hand-painted sign. Everyone knows your name because there are nine of them.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.blurb: Roads, a well, and the first traders who bother to stop. People are starting to talk.

tiers.name: Town
tiers.blurb: A market square, a garrison, and a name that carries a day's ride in every direction.

tiers.name: City
tiers.blurb: Walls you can see from the hills. Travelers now put you on their maps, and soon the map will put you on it.

tiers.name: Kingdom
tiers.blurb: Banners, borders, and neighbors who choose their words carefully. You are a power now, not a rumor.

tiers.name: Empire
tiers.blurb: A name spoken in other people's throne rooms. What you build, the world reacts to.

tiers.name: Ascendancy
tiers.blurb: Beyond borders, beyond rivals. History is written in the shape of what you leave behind.

buildings.name: House
buildings.blurb: Homes for the people. More room means more residents, and your headcount is your renown.

buildings.name: Solar Mine
buildings.blurb: Refines raw sunlight into hard currency. Your treasury's beating heart.

buildings.name: Lumber Camp
buildings.blurb: Fells and mills timber. Wood is the backbone of every early building, and its offcuts pile up as planks for the smith.

buildings.name: Quarry
buildings.blurb: Cuts stone from the bedrock. Slow, heavy, and needed by almost everything, and the ore-bearing spoil feeds the forge.

buildings.name: Iron Mine
buildings.blurb: Sinks shafts after iron. Expensive to run, but nothing high tier is built without it, and the deep veins throw off silver for the smith.

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.blurb: Bunks, a drill yard, and a quartermaster. Raises how many troops your empire can field.

buildings.name: Warehouse
buildings.blurb: Raises how much raw material your empire can stockpile before the surplus spoils.

buildings.name: Blacksmith
buildings.blurb: A resident smith and a roaring forge. Turns stashed materials into real gear, and the higher its level the rarer the work it can take on.

buildings.name: Bank
buildings.blurb: A counting house and a guarded vault. Your citizens store their own coin here, and the realm skims a small daily maintenance tax into the treasury.

buildings.name: Coffee House
buildings.blurb: A warm room, a long counter, and the smell of roasting beans. Folk gather here to sit a while, and every cup they order drops coin into the treasury.

menu.name: Solar Espresso
menu.line: A short, bright jolt of daylight. The room seems to sharpen for a moment.

menu.name: Comet Latte
menu.line: Warm and milky, gone too soon, like the tail of a comet.

menu.name: Void Cold Brew
menu.line: Dark enough to lose a small thought in. You feel wide awake.

menu.name: Astral Chai
menu.line: Spiced steam and a slow exhale. The day loosens its grip.

items.name: Gem Miner
items.blurb: A tireless little rig that chips a single gem loose every day, rain or shine.
items.detail: Once bought it's yours for good. Claim its find with *{prefix}empire premium claim* once every 24 hours, 💎1 per claim, no cap on how many days you keep it running.

items.name: Warehouse Permit
items.blurb: Deeds the crown recognizes without a single extra brick laid. Stacks with every other permit you hold.
items.detail: Instantly adds +50 permanent warehouse capacity to your empire. Buy as many as you like, each one stacks.

items.name: Rename Scroll
items.blurb: Strikes the old banners and raises new ones overnight, no questions asked.
items.detail: Renames your empire on the spot. Same rules as founding (3-20 characters, must be unique) but no solars, no rebuild.

_readme: Ready-to-assign preset empires. When a player's empire is lost, an owner
hands one of these over instead of rebuilding it by hand:
.empire preset            list the ladder
.empire preset <id>       inspect one in full
.empire preset suggest @player   pick the one that fits their level
.empire preset assign @player <id>
Headcount lives in `citizens`, which is written to record.npcs, NOT to
citizenCount. citizenCount is recomputed from the player side on every boot
(reconcileCitizenCount tallies u.empireId), so anything stored there is wiped.
fame and tierId are derived by ensureEmpireShape (fame = citizenCount + npcs),
so presets never set them.
Every preset is checked by scripts/empire-check.mjs: buildings within the
derived tier's buildingCap, army within armyCap, officers within officerCap,
warehouse within warehouseCap, and net solars per hour positive, so an
assigned empire funds its own upkeep and payroll from day one.
`soilerRank` is the top army rank the preset ships with (the ranked, tiered
soldier ladder), and producer building levels are set to match the same
scale, so both readings of the request are covered.
Presets above roughly 1,000 residents sit over their own popCap, so no new
townsfolk move in until the owner builds more housing. That is deliberate:
a handed-over empire arrives full, and growth is something the player earns.

list.name: Bronzevale Hollow
list.tagline: Timber, stone and grain. Wide open, cheap to run, easy to learn.
list.notes: Smallest preset. Best match for a player who was under level 40 or had a young empire.

list.name: Stonewatch March
list.tagline: Three barracks and a forge. No solar mine, this one lives off its people.
list.notes: For a player who cared about war and raids more than income.

list.name: Goldreach Basin
list.tagline: Five solar mines and a bank. Prints solars, thin on troops.
list.notes: For a player whose complaint was mostly lost solars. The mines earn it back instead of a hand out.

list.name: Ironhold Deeps
list.tagline: Three iron mines feeding two forges. Built to make gear, not coin.
list.notes: The forge preset. Best fit for anyone who lost armour or weapons and wants to reforge them.

list.name: Silkmoor Concord
list.tagline: Two banks, three coffee houses, warehouses stuffed to the rafters.
list.notes: The merchant preset. Deep storage, and the banks make it the best base for a market seller.

list.name: Ashen Bastion
list.tagline: Four barracks, a warlord, and iron enough to keep them all armed.
list.notes: Highest army power in the set. Give this to a player who ranked on the war board.

list.name: Verdantis Sprawl
list.tagline: Twelve housing blocks. The only preset with real room left to grow.
list.notes: Highest popCap of the set, so this one still takes new residents. Good for a player who wants to keep building.

list.name: Thronehold Ascendant
list.tagline: Every building type, twenty five of them, two warlords. The top of the set.
list.notes: Reserve this for the top of the old leaderboard. Hand it out sparingly, it outclasses anything a player can build in a week.
